title: Overcoming barriers to generalizability of deep learning for dental image analysis
summary:
Artificial intelligence (AI) can help dentists read dental images more accurately and consistently. This matters because small cavities or other lesions are easy to miss on X-rays or photos, and missed findings can delay treatment. However, many AI tools are trained on images from a single center. They may perform well where they were developed, but their accuracy often drops when used in other settings with different equipment or patient populations. This limited “generalizability” slows the safe use of AI in everyday care.
Our project aims to make dental AI reliable across various settings. We will use only de-identified images from several institutions (in Germany and abroad) to evaluate how well AI detects dental caries, apical (root-end) lesions, and oral mucosal lesions across different sites and imaging modalities. We will identify which factors (e.g., image quality, oral health status, or other data characteristics) cause performance to change. Then we will test practical ways to improve the reliability of AI predictions, with the goal of ensuring fair and clinically useful AI tools that work for patients wherever they receive dental care.
conditions: Dental caries, Apical periodontitis, Oral mucosal lesions

interventions.name: Multi-insitutional dataset of de-identified dental radiographs and intraoral photographs with associated metadata used for the development of AI models and an independent dataset used for external validation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
De-identified radiographs and intraoral photographs of adult humans.
Exclusion criteria:
Radiographs and intraoral photographs of insufficient quality or with major artifacts.
